properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): add_change_event has taken `repair`/`stands_in_for` since v0.68.0 (2026-09-23, #579). The reporter's 09-25 refusal came from an older server. Every instruction still routes the field elsewhere: root-cause step ⑧ names only snapshot_before_change (needs an arrived epoch and a target), and repair_report's served description names record_change, a REFUSING STUB since 2026-09-18
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL on dev_storyflow's 2026-09-25 entry (session 3bd108ab), triage of 2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED, verbatim: "the root-cause skill's step ⑧ says to mark the repair `corrected_cause` vs `contained_symptom`; `add_change_event` refuses `repair` ('unknown field') — only `snapshot_before_change` takes it, and that tool needs an epoch and a target node. So a plain fix recorded as a ChangeEvent cannot carry the one field the skill most wants. I wrote it into `summary`." Opportunity: "accept `repair`/`stands_in_for` on add_change_event".

② PRECEDENT: the field is cap:a-repair-says-which-kind-it-was / req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause. No earlier report of this refusal.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) TOOL — add_change_event lacks `repair` (the reporter's reading). (b) VERSION — the reporter's server predates the field on add_change_event. (c) INSTRUCTION — the tool takes it, and every instruction routes to another tool. (d) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG — a misspelt field.

④ DISCRIMINATOR: the committed toolsnaps at each tag, plus the current binary. (a) predicts no `repair` in add_change_event.json at v0.72.0. (b) predicts it appears at a tag cut before 09-25. (c) predicts the skill and repair_report still name another tool after that tag.

⑤ RESULT: add_change_event.json has no `repair`/`stands_in_for` at v0.66.0 or v0.67.0, and has both at v0.68.0 (tagged 2026-09-23), v0.71.0 and v0.72.0. They landed in #579 (9a3bbf0, 2026-09-23 17:17): "writable from add_change_event together with repair / stands_in_for (one shared validation with snapshot_before_change)". On 0.72.0, add_change_event{repair: contained_symptom, stands_in_for: …} was ACCEPTED, and repair_report counted it (contained_symptom 1, standing[] carries the sentence). A containment without stands_in_for was REFUSED with its reason. ⇒ (a) is REFUTED on the current release. (b) HOLDS: serde's "unknown field" is a server-side refusal, so the server answering on 09-25 predated v0.68.0. (c) HOLDS, measured three ways. [1] git log on getting-started/skills/root-cause/SKILL.md shows no change after b1118af (2026-09-23 05:04), which is BEFORE #579. So the step ⑧ the reporter read, and the one served today, says only "`snapshot_before_change` takes `repair`" (a mechanical rename of record_change in #535, 2026-09-18). snapshot_before_change refuses without an existing DesignEpoch (measured: "Node not found: DesignEpoch …"). [2] repair_report's served DESCRIPTION says "Write the disposition with `record_change`'s `repair` argument" in the toolsnaps at v0.67.0 AND v0.72.0. record_change is in DEPRECATED_TOOLS: called, it refuses and names snapshot_before_change (measured). #579 corrected repair_report's `note` output, not its description. [3] This capability's own description says "record_change takes a `repair` disposition", and add_change_event's tool description never mentions repair; only the parameter doc does.

⑥ CLASS: a field reached a second tool, and the three hand-kept places that route agents to it (the skill, a report's description, the capability prose) were never re-pointed, with nothing checking them against the surface. It is an instance of fact:root-cause-instructions-route-records-to-paths-that-cannot-take-them-and-the-lint-checks-names-only-2026-09-28. Would the class fix have prevented it? Yes. A check refusing any served description that names a DEPRECATED_TOOLS stub would have failed repair_report on 2026-09-18.

PINNING TEST (not written): no served skill or tool description names a tool in DEPRECATED_TOOLS (fails today on repair_report). And where a field is taken by more than one write tool, a skill instructing that field names the ordinary-path one (add_change_event for a plain fix).

THE REPORTER'S IDEA C-ii ("accept `repair`/`stands_in_for` on add_change_event") IS ALREADY BUILT, since v0.68.0, and is not minted as a Decision. What remains is re-pointing the instructions: step ⑧ naming add_change_event for a plain fix, repair_report's description, and this capability's prose. That is this finding's proposed fix.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: which binary storyflow ran on 09-25. The report names none; "at or before v0.67.0" is inferred from the refusal being server-side. Seven more served mentions of record_change exist (assure.rs:400, built.rs:369, query.rs:817, capture.rs:702/715/717/2191, temporal_tools.rs:535) and were not each triaged.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: "add_change_event refuses repair" was TRUE of their server and has been FALSE since v0.68.0. "that tool needs an epoch and a target node" HOLDS. "a plain fix recorded as a ChangeEvent cannot carry it" is OVERTURNED on the current release. An agent following the served skill today would still not find the route, because the skill does not name it.
